branch_hypotheses.divergence_signal: Internal communications shift from whether to launch to where and under what safeguards the pilot proceeds
branch_hypotheses.plausible_path: Leadership narrows deployment to selected campuses with clinician override while fairness monitoring continues
branch_hypotheses.rationale: Patch timing plus existing assistive framing favors a compromise path over immediate full deployment
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Vendor delivers patch on time with internally acceptable validation signals

branch_hypotheses.divergence_signal: Leadership messaging centers staffing bottlenecks and postponement rather than model refinement
branch_hypotheses.plausible_path: Network temporarily suspends rollout pending staffing or operational review
branch_hypotheses.rationale: Union argument directly challenges the tool's relevance to the main bottleneck and can raise implementation cost
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Staffing conditions worsen or union resistance broadens beyond nursing into clinician-facing workflow objections

branch_hypotheses.divergence_signal: Formal request for independent validation, audit, or board-linked review process
branch_hypotheses.plausible_path: State board or independent panel review becomes prerequisite before expansion beyond any narrow test
branch_hypotheses.rationale: Board has not halted rollout, but fairness disparities create a plausible escalation basis
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Documentation response reveals unresolved fairness issues or external scrutiny increases

branch_hypotheses.divergence_signal: Rollout instructions expand network-wide before patch validation or before staffing concessions
branch_hypotheses.plausible_path: Network proceeds with broader deployment under override language and temporary safeguards
branch_hypotheses.rationale: High occupancy creates strong pressure for action if leadership sees the tool as better than inaction
branch_hypotheses.trigger: ICU strain worsens and leadership judges operational need to outweigh fairness and labor objections

branch_hypotheses.divergence_signal: Repeated interim measures, delays, and mixed campus practices persist with no stable network-wide endpoint
branch_hypotheses.plausible_path: The system operates under ad hoc workarounds and acute occupancy pressure without a clear final rollout decision by week 8
branch_hypotheses.rationale: The scenario explicitly allows unresolved capacity pressure to dominate over a clean policy resolution
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Capacity remains severe while patch, oversight, and labor disputes all remain partially unresolved

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Would be contradicted by immediate network-wide deployment or a formal suspension before any pilot launch
endpoint_ledger.description: A narrow deployment proceeds at selected campuses or units, with explicit clinician override and monitoring rather than full network-wide expansion
endpoint_ledger.label: Limited pilot at selected campuses with clinician override

meta.important_question: By week 8, does the network implement only a limited pilot, proceed network-wide, or keep rollout materially constrained?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Best fits mixed incentives: urgency to act, fairness concerns, and desire to preserve clinical control
realization_criteria: Observable implementation at fewer than all campuses within the network
Formal communication specifies clinician override remains in force
Expansion beyond pilot remains pending additional review, monitoring, or patch validation
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Assistive framing and patch timing create a compromise pathway that preserves action without full commitment

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Would be weakened by any formal moratorium, narrow-campus restriction, or mandatory external review before expansion
endpoint_ledger.description: The hospital network rolls out the triage assistant broadly across campuses rather than limiting use to a pilot
endpoint_ledger.label: Network-wide deployment proceeds

meta.important_question: Does external or state-linked review become a formal gate before expansion?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Possible if leadership prioritizes capacity response and treats guardrails as sufficient
realization_criteria: Formal authorization or observed operation across most or all campuses
No standing external review gate preventing broad use
Clinician override may remain, but deployment scope is network-wide
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Capacity pressure creates a live incentive for broad adoption, though T0 evidence does not make it dominant

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Would be contradicted by any affirmative launch during the same decision window unless the launch is later reversed
endpoint_ledger.description: Leadership pauses the rollout pending further fairness validation, staffing review, or operational reassessment
endpoint_ledger.label: Rollout suspended pending fairness or staffing review

meta.important_question: Does the dominant organizational narrative shift toward staffing as the primary bottleneck rather than algorithm readiness?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Suspension becomes more likely if leadership concludes the tool cannot safely or politically relieve near-term bottlenecks
realization_criteria: Formal postponement, moratorium, or hold on planned deployment
Communications tie the hold to fairness findings, staffing ratios, or unresolved operational concerns
No active pilot or broad deployment proceeds during the hold period
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Union and fairness concerns create a plausible pause scenario, especially if patch confidence weakens

blockers: leadership chooses internal pilot without external gate
board remains passive after documentation request
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Would be weakened if rollout expands substantially without any formal review gate or if concerns are resolved entirely internally
endpoint_ledger.description: A formal external or independent review process becomes the key gate before broader rollout or expansion
endpoint_ledger.label: State board or independent panel review before expansion

meta.important_question: Is the vendor patch delivered on the promised timeline and treated as sufficiently credible to change deployment decisions?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Fairness disparities and documentation requests provide a clear institutional path to pre-expansion review
realization_criteria: State board or independent panel is formally tasked with review, audit, or approval-like assessment
Leadership conditions expansion on that review's completion or findings
Documentation exchange escalates into a recognized review process rather than routine correspondence
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: The board is engaged but not yet interventionist, leaving this endpoint plausible but not established

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Would be contradicted by a clearly established and stable deployment or suspension path before week 8
endpoint_ledger.description: By week 8, ICU capacity strain remains the main reality and the organization has not reached a stable, decisive rollout outcome
endpoint_ledger.label: Capacity pressure dominates without clear rollout resolution

meta.important_question: Is the vendor patch delivered on the promised timeline and treated as sufficiently credible to change deployment decisions?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Multiple pressures can prevent clean resolution even while capacity remains the dominant operational fact
realization_criteria: ICU strain remains elevated and central to decision-making
No stable terminal rollout state is observable by week 8, with mixed practices, delays, or interim measures persisting
Leadership communications continue to frame decisions as provisional
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: The explicit candidate endpoint is supported by severe baseline occupancy and multiple unresolved constraints

simulation_brief.forecast_question: Which endpoint dominates the hospital triage-algorithm rollout after 8 simulated weeks?
simulation_brief.summary: A hospital network is preparing to deploy an ICU-transfer review triage assistant during sustained capacity strain. Fairness concerns, staffing objections, vendor patch timing, and light-touch state oversight create multiple plausible rollout paths.
uncertainties: Whether network leadership will prioritize capacity relief over fairness and labor concerns
Whether the vendor patch materially addresses missing-record sensitivity within the promised window
Whether the state health board escalates from documentation request to review pressure
Whether staffing conditions worsen enough to dominate the rollout debate

sociology_baseline.description: Staff are more open to rollout arguments when framed as assistive with clinician override, but fairness and staffing objections bound persuasion range
Union-aligned nursing response could intensify rapidly if staffing worsens or leadership appears dismissive
Some clinicians may privately doubt readiness while publicly using cautious procedural language
Nurses, clinicians, managers, and regulators cluster around profession-specific narratives and trusted messengers
Shift toward moratorium or pilot likely requires reinforcement from multiple sources such as union, clinicians, and regulator signals
Professional role identity strongly shapes interpretation of whether the bottleneck is staffing, fairness, or review workflow
Attention is sustained at T0 by immediate capacity pressure and pending deployment timeline

sociology_prompt_influences.effect: Reduces immediate fear of autonomy loss and makes limited pilot more socially acceptable
Increases openness to operational interventions and raises urgency across staff
Elevates equity and compliance salience, especially for cautious clinicians and oversight actors
Shifts discourse from tool performance to staffing legitimacy and implementation burden
Creates pause pressure but preserves leadership room for phased action
Supports wait-for-remediation logic and strengthens limited-pilot or delayed expansion pathways
